reasons: Lake identity verifies Timbs v. Indiana as a U.S. Supreme Court decision decided 2019-02-20 with docket No. 17-1091.
Lake citations verify official cite 586 U.S. 146, parallel cites 139 S. Ct. 682 and 203 L. Ed. 2d 11, and vendor-neutral cite 2019 U.S. LEXIS 1350.
No disclosed treatment edge says the decision was overruled, abrogated, superseded, or limited.
residual_risks: The lake treatment record is unverified and has no citator/progeny enumeration, so live-law status beyond disclosed records is not proven.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep any live-law implication tied to the visible Treatment: Unverified caveat.

reasons: Currency/treatment lens discloses no adverse treatment that would make the Civil Asset Forfeiture anchor role untenable.
Support classification itself is outside lens B, and no treatment defect appears in the disclosed lake fields.
residual_risks: Treatment remains unverified, so the role should not be read as a verified good-law signal.

defect.problem: The holding is phrased in present-tense doctrinal terms, but the disclosed lake treatment fields do not verify current good-law status.
defect.proposed_fix: Recast as a historical holding, e.g., "Timbs held that...", or add an explicit treatment caveat that current citator status is unverified.

reasons: The opinion text verifies that Timbs announced the incorporation holding, but lens B asks whether the asserted rule remains live law.
The lake treatment record states field_i_validity and composite_basis are unverified, as_of_treatment is null, and edges are empty.
Defaulting to refuted/modified on currency uncertainty, the assertion should not be presented as verified current doctrine without the unverified-treatment caveat.
residual_risks: A completed citator/progeny review may confirm the same rule; that evidence is not present in the disclosed record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Phrase this field as the case's historical holding until treatment is promoted.

reasons: The content treatment payload matches the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity unverified, as_of_content null, as_of_treatment null, composite_basis unverified, varies_by_point false.
The lake scope note states that treatment/progeny were intentionally not derived until S6 promotion.
The disclosed treatment edges array is empty, so there is no contrary disclosed adverse-treatment call.
residual_risks: Because treatment is unverified, this is not a good-law certification.

reasons: Lake identity verifies court_level scotus and court U.S. Supreme Court, supporting the source-weight label Binding — SCOTUS.
No disclosed treatment edge supersedes, overrules, abrogates, or limits Timbs in a way that would contradict the weight label.
The separate treatment field correctly remains unverified, so the weight label is not itself a citator status.
residual_risks: If the corpus uses Binding — SCOTUS to imply current validity rather than court hierarchy, the unverified treatment field would need promotion before that implication is safe.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Maintain a clear distinction between court-level weight and verified good-law status.
